A no-break space immediately after the colon is also outside the covered-whitespace class and is explicitly rejected (not merely left unconsumed), closing the case where the ordinary Unicode-\s-aware tokenizer would otherwise still treat it as a separator and rescue 'Go'.

Correction regression (Sol's finding): a punctuation run followed by a no-break space must still end the region, exactly like ASCII space would -- not be skipped as 'not genuine', which previously let the region extend across the clause boundary and wrongly rescue standalone 'Go'.

Positive control neighboring the two NBSP regressions above: an ordinary ASCII space after the period still ends the region exactly where it always did, proving the fix did not change the already-correct covered-whitespace case.

A vertical tab (plain ASCII whitespace, but outside this module's own covered-whitespace class) after the period must also end the region, proving the fix is not narrowly special-cased to the no-break space alone.
A form feed after the period must also end the region, for the same reason as the vertical-tab case.

Python does not match here either, because the invisible format character glues 'Python.' and 'When' into one unmatched token in the ordinary whole-text pass -- a separate, pre-existing tokenizer property unrelated to and unaffected by this region-boundary fix.
